span.label: On about 6% of trials where the primed response was correctly made, subjects also made an extra unrequired response, and nearly every extra response used the other hand, indicating that the opposite-hand response had also been readied.

span.label: Reaction times were longer when only the finger had to change from the primed response than when both finger and hand had to change, the opposite of what a simple feature-specification account predicts.

span.label: The method's core assumption failed in part of the experiment: subjects readied nonprimed responses alongside the primed one in some conditions, which blocked full use of the method's inferential machinery.

span.label: The proposed pair of preparation methods reconciles the opposite within-hand and between-hand advantages found across experiments, at the cost of assuming that same-hand responses share more movement features than opposite-hand responses.
